Law: The Constitution of Pakistan, 1973: Article 25 guarantees equality before law and equal protection of law, prohibiting discrimination on the basis of sex. Article 25(2) allows the state to make special provisions for the protection of women and children.
The Protection against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010: This act prohibits gender-based discrimination and harassment at workplaces and provides mechanisms for redressal.

The Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act, 2016: This act provides protection against various forms of violence and discrimination against women, including economic and social discrimination.
The Sindh Protection of Women against Violence Act, 2013: Similar to the Punjab act, this provides protection against violence and discrimination in Sindh province.
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Protection of Women against Violence Act, 2017: Provides legal framework for protection against violence and discrimination in KPK province.
The Balochistan Protection of Women against Violence Act, 2014: Provides protection mechanisms against violence and discrimination in Balochistan province.
The Equal Remuneration Act (if applicable): Ensures equal pay for equal work regardless of gender, though Pakistan's implementation varies.
The Employment of Children Act, 1991: While primarily about child labor, it includes provisions that affect gender equality in employment.
The Maternity Benefits Ordinance, 1958: Provides maternity benefits to working women, addressing gender-specific workplace needs.
The Factories Act, 1934: Includes provisions for equal treatment of workers regardless of gender in factory settings.
The West Pakistan Maternity Benefit Act, 1958: Provides maternity leave and benefits to protect women's employment rights during pregnancy.
The National Commission on the Status of Women Act, 2012: Establishes a commission to monitor and evaluate policies related to women's rights and gender equality.
The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2016: Includes provisions addressing gender-based violence and discrimination.

The Prevention of Anti-Women Practices (Criminal Law Amendment) Act, 2011: Criminalizes various discriminatory practices against women including forced marriage, denial of inheritance, and other harmful customs.
